#Part 1
1.Open the sleep dataset in R
```{r}
data(sleep)
library(tidyverse)
```

2. Is it long or wide format? How do you know?
  Long. Only 10 patients but 20 observations so each patient has multiple rows of data, making it long.
3. Transform this data so that it is in the other format.
```{r}
sleep_wide <- pivot_wider(sleep, names_from = group, values_from = extra)
```

4. Transform your data back to its original format.
```{r}
sleep_long <- pivot_longer(sleep_wide, cols = c("1", "2"), names_to = "group", values_to = "extra")
```

5. Open the Starwars dataset
```{r}
data(starwars)
```

6. Create homeworld as a factor. How many levels does it have?
```{r}
starwars$homeworld2 <- as.factor(starwars$homeworld)
levels(starwars$homeworld2)
nlevels(starwars$homeworld2)
#48 levels
```

7. Reorder homeworld so that Naboo is the reference group.
```{r}
starwars$homeworld2 <- relevel(starwars$homeworld2, ref = "Naboo")
levels(starwars$homeworld2)
```

8. Use mutate to create a column transforming kg to pounds. (hint: you may need to look up the conversion)
```{r}
starwars<- starwars |> mutate(massLbs = mass*2.2)
```

9. Print a summary of your column from #8
```{r}
summary(starwars$massLbs)
```


#Part 2
10. open the billboard dataset.
```{r}
data(billboard)
```

11. are the data in this dataframe in long or wide format? explain how you know.
  Wide. Each song has only 1 row, the wide columns are the weeks with weekly rankings for each song
12. change the data from its original format to the other version.
```{r}
billboardLong<- pivot_longer(billboard, cols = starts_with("wk"), names_to = "week", names_prefix = "wk", values_to = "rank")

# i wanted to find a way to shorten the process of selecting each column without writing each individual column. i found https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/pivot_longer.html for starts_with, which will use the columns that start with "wk" (which is every single weekly column) and also to remove the "wk" using names_prefix. names_prefix would then only select everything after "wk" to copy into the new columns, from the ? page:  regular expression used to remove matching text from the start of each variable name.
```

13. change it from your altered version in #3 back to its original state.
```{r}
billboardWide <- pivot_wider(billboardLong, names_from = "week", values_from = "rank", names_prefix = "wk")
```

14. Separate the date entered column into three columns: one for year, one for month, and one for day.
```{r}
dateSeparateBillboard <- separate(billboard, date.entered, into = c("Year", "Month", "Date"), sep = "-")
```
